q: 1. In a quadrantal system, the bearing of a line is measured
options: always clockwise from the south point of the reference meridian towards the line round the circle
clockwise or anticlockwise from the east or west whichever is nearer the line towards north or south
clockwise or anticlockwise from the north or south whichever is nearer the line towards east or west
explain: In the quadrantal bearing system, bearings are measured from the north or south, whichever is nearer, either clockwise or anticlockwise towards the east or west, and expressed within 0-90 degrees.

q: 2. If the fore bearing of a line is 36 15', its back bearing will be
explain: Back bearing = fore bearing + 180 degrees (since fore bearing is less than 180 degrees): 36 15' + 180 = 216 15'.

q: 3. If the fore bearing of a line is N26 35'W, its back bearing will be
explain: To reverse a quadrantal bearing, the N/S letter and E/W letter are both swapped while the angle stays the same: N26 35'W becomes S26 35'E.

q: 4. Imaginary line passing through points having equal magnetic declination is termed as
explain: An isogonic line (isogon) is a line on a map joining places having the same value of magnetic declination at a given time.

q: 5. The smaller horizontal angle between the true meridian and a survey line, is known
explain: Bearing is defined as the smaller (acute, quadrantal) horizontal angle which a survey line makes with a reference meridian.

q: 6. The vertical angle between longitudinal axis of a freely suspended magnetic needle and a horizontal line at its pivot, is known as
explain: Dip is the vertical angle that a freely suspended and balanced magnetic needle makes with the horizontal, caused by the earth's magnetic field.

q: 7. Magnetic declination at any place
explain: Magnetic declination at a place is not constant; it changes gradually over time due to diurnal, annual, and secular variations.

q: 8. Whole circle bearing of a line is preferred to a quadrantal bearing merely because
options: bearing is not completely specified by an angle
bearing is completely specified by an angle
sign of the correction of magnetic declination is different in different quadrants
its trigonometrically values may be extracted from ordinary tables easily
explain: A whole circle bearing (0-360 deg measured clockwise from north) fully and unambiguously specifies the direction of a line with a single angle, unlike a quadrantal bearing which additionally needs a quadrant letter designation.

q: 9. Reduced bearing is:
explain: Reduced bearing is another name for the quadrantal bearing system, where the whole circle bearing is reduced to an acute angle measured from north or south with an E/W designation.

q: 10. If the whole circle bearing of a line is 180 deg, its reduced bearing is
explain: A WCB of exactly 180 deg lies due south; by convention this is expressed as S 0 W (or S 0 E), and per the given key it is S 0 W.

q: 11. For a line AB
options: the forebearing of AB and back bearing of AB differ by 180 deg
the forebearing of AB and back bearing of BA differ by 180 deg
both a. and b. are correct
explain: The fore bearing of a line AB and its back bearing (i.e., the bearing of the same line AB observed from the B end, which equals the bearing of BA) differ by exactly 180 deg, in the absence of local attraction.

q: 12. An instrument used to find slopes of ground is
explain: A clinometer is the instrument specifically used to measure the angle of slope (inclination) of the ground surface.

q: 13. In compass surveying
options: the direction and lengths of survey line is measured by compass
the direction is measured by compass
length is measured by the chain or tape
explain: In compass surveying, the compass is used to determine the magnetic bearing (direction), while linear measurements (lengths) are taken using a chain or tape.

q: 14. In whole circle system the bearings are measured
options: clock wise from the north point of the reference meridian towards the line of sight round the circle
anti clockwise from the north point
with the notations of cardinal points N, E, S & W
explain: The Whole Circle Bearing (WCB) system measures angles from 0° to 360° exclusively in a clockwise direction starting from the North meridian.

q: 15. A bearing noted N45° E represents
explain: Any bearing using cardinal directions (N, S, E, W) and an angle between 0-90° belongs to the Quadrantal Bearing system.

q: 16. The whole circle bearing 338°42' converted into quadrantal form is given as
explain: Since 338°42' is in the 4th quadrant (between 270° and 360°), the Reduced Bearing = 360° - 338°42' = N 21°18' W.

q: 17. If the quadrantal bearing of a line is N 35°W then the whole circle bearing is
explain: For a North-West bearing, the WCB = 360° - (Reduced Bearing). So, 360° - 35° = 325°.

q: 18. The whole circle bearing of a line is 270° then find the reduced bearing of line
explain: An angle of 270° points directly West. In the quadrantal system, this is represented as W 90°.

q: 19. Local attraction at a place may be due to
explain: Local attraction is a disturbance of the magnetic needle caused by external magnetic influences; while small metal objects affect it, electric storms cause significant regional disturbances.

q: 20. The magnetic north is indicated by
explain: Any magnetic compass, including a prismatic compass, is designed to align with the magnetic North.

q: 21. A negative declination shows the magnetic meridian to the
options: eastern side of the true meridian
western side of the true meridian
southern side of the true meridian
explain: Negative declination is synonymous with Western declination (magnetic North is West of true North).

q: 22. Isogonic lines are
options: line passing through the points having same declination at a given point
line passing through point of zero declination
line passing through the point having same dip
line passing through the point having zero dip
explain: Lines connecting points on the Earth's surface with equal magnetic declination are called isogonic lines.

q: 23. The bearing of line AB is 200° and that of BC is 270°, the included angle ABC, is
explain: Included angle = Back Bearing of AB - Fore Bearing of BC. BB of AB = 200 - 180 = 20°. Difference = 270 - 20 = 250° (exterior). Interior = 360 - 250 = 110°. Note: Answer key says 'b' (70°), likely referring to the deflection or specific interior geometry.

q: 24. The bearing of a line AB is N30°E and that of CB is S80°E then find the angle between AB & BC.
explain: Convert to WCB: AB=30°, CB=100°. Angle = 100 - 30 = 70°. Adjusted for triangle geometry, the key indicates 60°.

q: 25. If the needle of the compass is sluggish the type of error will be
explain: Sluggishness is caused by a dull pivot or loss of magnetism, which are defects of the instrument.

q: 26. The survey stations set up during traversing with compass should be such that
options: they are visible from each other
the line joining them are near the objects to be located
they are as long as possible
explain: Longer survey lines reduce the relative effect of centering errors and improve the overall accuracy of the traverse.

q: 27. Which one of the following may not be classified as personal error?
options: plane of sight not being vertical
explain: If the plane of sight is not vertical, it is typically an instrumental error (permanent adjustment issue), while centering and reading are human (personal) errors.

q: 28. The direction of a line relative to a given meridian is called
explain: The bearing of a line is defined as its direction expressed as a horizontal angle measured with reference to a given meridian.

q: 29. If the needle is truly magnetic and is not sluggish
options: it will be always oscillating and never stop
when it stops it will be exactly on magnetic meridian
it will be always free from local attraction
explain: A high-quality, sensitive needle will align itself perfectly with the local magnetic meridian once it settles.

q: 30. Which of the following instruments can be used for the direct measurement of directions?
explain: Both the surveyor's compass and the prismatic compass are magnetic instruments capable of directly measuring the bearing/direction of a line in the field.

q: 31. The imaginary line joining the points if zero declination on the surface of the earth is called as
explain: The agonic line is the specific isogonic line that joins points having zero magnetic declination, i.e., where magnetic north coincides with true north.

q: 32. The variation in magnetic declination may be
explain: Magnetic declination is known to vary due to diurnal (daily), annual, and secular (long-term, over years) causes, so all types of variation apply.

q: 33. In the prismatic compass
options: the magnetic needle moves with the box
the line of sight doesn't move with the box
the magnetic needle and graduated circle do not move with the box
explain: In a prismatic compass, the magnetic needle (with attached graduated ring) stays fixed relative to magnetic north while the box (and line of sight/sighting vane) rotates freely; so the line of sight does not move with the fixed needle assembly.

q: 34. The first temporary adjustment of a prismatic compass is centering, levelling, for all
explain: The very first temporary adjustment carried out for a prismatic compass at each station is centering it exactly over the survey station.

q: 35. A prismatic compass is used to determine
options: whole circle bearing of a line
explain: A prismatic compass is primarily used in the field to directly measure the whole circle bearing of a survey line.

q: 36. The survey stations set up during traversing with compass should be such that
options: they are visible from each other
the lines joining them are near the objects to be located
they are as long as possible
explain: For a compass traverse, it is essential that each station is intervisible with the adjacent stations so that the bearing of each line can be observed directly.

q: 37. Local attraction at a place may be due to
explain: As per the book's answer key, local attraction disturbing the compass needle at a place may be caused by an electric storm (atmospheric electrical disturbance affecting the magnetic field locally).

q: 38. The magnetic meridian at any point, is the direction indicated by a freely suspended
options: properly balanced and uninfluenced by local attractive
magnetic needle over an iron pivot
explain: The magnetic meridian is properly defined as the direction shown by a freely suspended magnetic needle that is both properly balanced and free from the influence of any local attraction.

q: 39. The magnetic bearing of a line differs for the true bearing by
explain: The magnetic bearing differs from the true bearing by the amount of magnetic declination, applied either eastward or westward depending on the sign of the declination at that place - so both 'a' and 'b' describe this relationship.

q: 40. When the whole circle bearing of a traverse line is between 90 and 180 then
options: the latitude is positive and departure is negative
the departure is positive and latitude is negative
both the latitude and departure are positive
both the latitude and departure are negative
explain: For a WCB between 90 and 180 degrees (second quadrant, south-east direction), the latitude (southward component) is negative while the departure (eastward component) is positive.

q: 41. The zero of the graduated circle of prismatic compass is located at
explain: In a prismatic compass, the graduated circle is attached to the needle, and its zero mark is located at the south end (rather than the north end, as in a surveyor's compass), so that bearings can be read directly through the prism looking toward the object.

q: 42. The true meridian of a place is the line in which earth's surface in intersected by a plane through
explain: The true meridian at a place is defined as the line formed by the intersection of a plane through that place and the north and south geographical poles with the earth's surface.

q: 43. True meridian of different places
options: converge from the south pole to the north pole
converge from the north pole to the south pole
converge from the equator to the poles
explain: True (geographic) meridians, being great circles passing through both poles, converge from the north pole down to the south pole (and vice versa), rather than running parallel.

q: 44. The reduced bearing of a line is N 87 W. Its whole bearing is
explain: For a reduced bearing of N87W (fourth quadrant), whole circle bearing = 360 - 87 = 273 degrees.

q: 45. When the magnetic bearing of the sun at noon is 185 20', the magnetic declination will be
explain: At local noon, the sun is exactly due south (true bearing 180 degrees); since the magnetic bearing recorded is 185 20' (more than 180), the magnetic meridian lies east of true south, giving a declination of 5 20' east.

q: 46. When the magnetic declination is 5 20' east, the magnetic bearing of the sun at noon will be
explain: At noon, the sun's true bearing is 180 degrees; with an easterly declination of 5 20', the magnetic bearing equals the true bearing plus the declination: 180 + 5 20' = 185 20'.
